name: Dr.ICL: Demonstration-Retrieved In-context Learning
venue: Data Intelligence, Vol. 6, Issue 4, pp. 909-922 (2024 acceptance; published 2025-03-03; DOI 10.3724/2096-7004.di.2024.0012); originally arXiv:2305.14128 (May 2023)
authors_affiliation: Man Luo (Arizona State University), Xin Xu, Zhuyun Dai, Panupong Pasupat, Mehran Kazemi, Vaiva Imbrasaite, Vincent Y. Zhao (Google Research), Chitta Baral (Arizona State University). Lead author Man Luo; primary affiliations Arizona State University and Google Research.
code_url: N/A (no official code repository is linked in the paper or arXiv listing; no public release found)
task_domain: QA and NLP reasoning: free-form question answering, natural language inference, mathematical reasoning, and boolean/commonsense QA. This is an in-context-learning / demonstration-retrieval study, not an agent/tool-use/planning system.
problem_setting: Offline, single-turn in-context learning (ICL) with frozen large LLMs (no parameter updates). For each test query the system retrieves query-specific few-shot demonstrations from the labeled training set of the same task and prepends them to the prompt. Supervision is available in the form of the task's training data (used both as the demonstration pool and to mine training signal for a learned retriever). Settings cover one-shot and few-shot ICL, with both a general LLM (PaLM) and an instruction-finetuned LLM (Flan-PaLM), and with Chain-of-Thought (CoT) prompting for reasoning tasks. Single-agent; no interactive environment.
what_is_retrieved: Demonstrations (few-shot exemplars), i.e. labeled (input, answer) pairs from the task training data; for CoT tasks the demonstrations contain intermediate reasoning chains.
retrieval_grounding: STATIC external corpus: the fixed, labeled task training set (Dtrain) is the demonstration pool. No growing/episodic memory; the store does not change during inference.
completeness_vs_topk_objective: Fixed top-k (top-n) ranking objective: a retriever selects the n most relevant demonstrations per query (n=1 for one-shot, fixed n for few-shot). There is no completeness/minimal-set objective and no precision-driven variable-size selection. The task description's claim of 'diverse-coverage selection (Dr.ICL/Cover-LS)' is NOT supported by this paper; Dr.ICL uses similarity-based top-n retrieval, not diverse-coverage set selection, and 'Cover-LS' does not appear in the paper.
cbr_cycle_coverage: Retrieve: yes; Reuse: yes (verbatim in-context exemplars); Revise: no; Retain: no. [Retrieve, Reuse]
explicit_cbr_grounding: False. The work frames itself as retrieval-based in-context learning (Dr.ICL) and does not cite or invoke case-based reasoning (Aamodt & Plaza / Kolodner). Verbatim exemplar reuse loosely resembles CBR Retrieve+Reuse but is not framed as CBR.
retrieval_unit: Single demonstration = a (problem, solution) / (input, answer) pair; for CoT tasks the demonstration also includes a step-by-step reasoning chain. Granularity is one full labeled example per retrieved item.
index_source: Static corpus built offline from the existing task training data (Dtrain). The retrievable store is the same labeled training pool used at train time; it is frozen at test time (no online/test-time induction). For the trained retriever, additional offline mining produces positive/hard-negative pairs, but the demonstration pool itself stays static.
index_structure_topology: Flat index. BM25 uses a sparse bag-of-words inverted index; GTR / the trained Demo-GTR use a flat dense vector index (dual-encoder embeddings with inner-product / nearest-neighbor search). No graph, hierarchy, or clustering.
retriever_type: Three variants: (1) BM25 (sparse, off-the-shelf), (2) GTR (dense dual-encoder based on T5, off-the-shelf), and (3) Demo-GTR, a learned dense retriever fine-tuned from GTR. Hybrid in the sense that both sparse and dense off-the-shelf retrievers are studied plus a trained one.
retriever_learning_signal: Two regimes. Off-the-shelf BM25/GTR: none (no task-specific training). Trained Demo-GTR: LM-feedback / downstream-task-effectiveness signal — for each training query, GTR retrieves 100 candidate demonstrations, PaLM-62B scores each by the LM probability p_LM(y_q | d, x_q) of the gold answer, the top-n are positives and bottom-n hard negatives, and GTR is fine-tuned with a contrastive (InfoNCE) loss using in-batch and hard negatives.
query_construction: Raw input query used directly as the retrieval key: the test question/input x_q is matched against candidate demonstrations in the training pool. No decomposition, sub-queries, or synthetic query expansion. For CoT tasks demonstrations carry reasoning chains and retrieval is based on the query (and, per the published version, retrieving based on reasoning chains gives improvements).
query_granularity: Task-level / one-shot at t=0: a single retrieval is performed per test query before generation; there is no per-step or trajectory-level re-querying.
when_to_retrieve: One-shot (single retrieval per query before the LLM call). Not iterative, active, or adaptively routed.
retrieval_trigger_signal: Fixed schedule: retrieval always happens once per test query prior to prompting. No confidence-, uncertainty-, classifier-, or agent-initiated trigger.
reranking: For the off-the-shelf inference pipeline, no separate reranking stage at test time (top-n nearest demonstrations are used directly). During training-data construction for Demo-GTR, an LLM (PaLM-62B) reranks the GTR-retrieved 100 candidates by gold-answer probability to mine positives/hard-negatives — a training-time reranking, not an inference-time reranker.
retrieved_context_refinement: None. Retrieved demonstrations are inserted into the prompt as-is (linearized as 'question: x \n answer: y', with reasoning chains for CoT). No decomposition, distillation, compression, or distractor filtering.
tool_document_engineering: N/A (no tools; demonstrations are raw labeled examples, not engineered tool/skill descriptions).
index_content_separation: N/A / No. There is no lightweight-index-then-heavy-content separation; demonstrations are both the index entries and the injected content.
dynamic_index_and_protocol: N/A (no tool index, no live synchronization, no MCP/RapidAPI/function-calling protocol).
tool_dependency_awareness: N/A (no tools; no inter-tool dependency modeling).
how_retrieved_used: Prompt augmentation: the retrieved demonstrations are prepended to the test query as few-shot in-context exemplars; the frozen LLM conditions on them to predict the answer. For Demo-GTR, retrieval feedback (LM scores) is also used as a training signal to learn the retriever, but at inference the retrieved demos are used purely as prompt context.
planning_integration: N/A for planning/acting. The closest mapping is one-shot exemplars injected at prompt/generation time (retrieve-then-generate). There is no MCTS, tree search, hierarchical subtask planning, or per-step interleaving; for reasoning tasks, retrieved CoT demonstrations guide a single forward generation.
reasoning_search_interleaving_granularit: Per-answer: retrieval occurs once and the full answer (including any CoT) is generated in a single pass. Retrieval is not interleaved per CoT step or per token.
adaptation_mechanism: Verbatim ICL exemplar: retrieved cases are reused as-is in the prompt with no adaptation/revision step. (CBR-style 'Revise' is absent.)
retrieved_item_representation: Raw demonstration text: linearized (input, answer) pairs, including raw step-by-step reasoning chains for CoT tasks. No distillation into strategies, programs, or latent tokens.
abstraction_level_of_retrieved_unit: Single demonstration (concrete labeled example). For CoT tasks the demonstration includes a raw reasoning trajectory, but it is still a concrete worked example rather than a distilled strategy, workflow, or skill.
noise_robustness_mechanism: Limited. The main mechanism is training a task-specific retriever (Demo-GTR) on LM-feedback with hard negatives so that more task-representative (less merely query-overlapping) demonstrations are retrieved, reducing unhelpful exemplars. The paper also analyzes label/answer overlap (Table 3) to confirm gains are not due to trivial label copying. No explicit relevance evaluator, self-reflection, or reason-in-documents filtering at inference.
memory_type: none (static labeled training pool; no episodic/skill/workflow/procedural/graph/latent memory).
write_back: False. The system never writes new experiences/cases/skills back into a memory store; the demonstration pool is the fixed training set.
online_growth: No. The retrievable store is frozen after offline construction; it does not grow during deployment/test-time.
failure_experience_usage: Success-only at inference (only gold labeled demonstrations are retrieved/used). During offline training of Demo-GTR, low-utility demonstrations (lowest LM-probability candidates) are used as HARD NEGATIVES in the contrastive loss, so 'unhelpful' examples inform retriever training, but there is no storage/retrieval of failed agent trajectories.
memory_evolution_update: N/A / append-only static (no entries are mutated; the pool is fixed and not updated post hoc).
retrieval_as_learned_policy: Partially: Demo-GTR is a learned (contrastively trained) retriever optimized via LM-feedback-derived labels, which is more than fixed similarity top-k. However it is a learned similarity/relevance scorer, NOT an RL/value-based sequential policy (no M-MDP, soft Q-learning, or interactive preference optimization). The BM25/GTR variants are fixed similarity top-k.
cross_agent_or_cross_framework_sharing: N/A / No. Single-LLM, single-task setting; no cross-agent or cross-framework memory/experience sharing.
benchmarks: NQ (Natural Questions, free-form QA), ANLI round 3 / ANLI-r3 (natural language inference), GSM8k (grade-school math word problems, with CoT), AQuA (algebraic word problems with multiple choice, with CoT), StrategyQA (boolean/multi-hop commonsense QA, with CoT). Five datasets total.
benchmark_family: QA (NQ, StrategyQA), NLI (ANLI-r3), and math reasoning (GSM8k, AQuA). No web/embodied/tool/code/memory/decision-RL agent benchmarks.
baselines: Random demonstrations and no-demonstration (zero-shot) prompting; off-the-shelf retrievers BM25 and GTR. The trained Demo-GTR retriever is compared against off-the-shelf GTR. Related-work methods (KATE, EPR, CEIL, UPRISE) are discussed for positioning but not all directly re-run as head-to-head baselines.
key_metrics: Exact-match accuracy on all five tasks (downstream task accuracy). No separate Recall@k / nDCG retrieval metrics are reported.
headline_result: Retrieved demonstrations (BM25 or GTR) beat random demonstrations for both PaLM-540B and Flan-PaLM across one-shot and few-shot settings; and the trained Demo-GTR retriever further beats off-the-shelf GTR, e.g. PaLM one-shot average accuracy rises from 49.8 (GTR) to 51.1 (Demo-GTR, +1.3), with per-task one-shot gains NQ 37.8->39.2 (+1.4), ANLI-r3 54.0->54.8 (+0.8), GSM8k 57.7->59.3 (+1.6); improvements are largest in the one-shot setting.
ablations: Comparison of demonstration source (no-demo vs random vs BM25 vs GTR) across one-shot and few-shot for both PaLM and Flan-PaLM (Figures 3-4), isolating that retrieval (vs random) drives gains and that even sparse BM25 helps. Off-the-shelf GTR vs trained Demo-GTR (Table 2) isolates the value of the learned retriever, especially in one-shot. Answer-overlap analysis (Table 3) ablates whether gains come from trivial label/answer leakage, finding overlap ratios near/below the uniform-label baseline for four of five datasets (NQ is the exception, with notable answer overlap explained by near-duplicate questions). The retriever-training recipe uses GTR to fetch 100 candidates, PaLM-62B to score, and top-5 reranked as positives.
evaluation_decoupling: No. Only end-to-end exact-match accuracy is reported; intrinsic retrieval metrics (Recall@k/nDCG) are not reported separately.
process_vs_outcome_metrics: Primarily outcome (final exact-match accuracy). Some process-oriented analysis is provided qualitatively (answer/label overlap analysis and inspection of retrieved demonstrations) but no quantitative step-wise reasoning-faithfulness or retrieval-quality scoring.
cost_efficiency_tradeoff: Discussed qualitatively: BM25 is highlighted as efficient in indexing memory and retrieval latency and easy to deploy at scale relative to dense semantic retrievers (GTR); the trained retriever's gains are largest in the one-shot setting, which needs less inference latency/compute than few-shot. No precise latency/throughput/API-cost numbers are reported.
context_budget_and_selection_count: Fixed-k: one-shot (k=1) and few-shot (fixed small k, not exhaustively specified per task) demonstrations selected by top-n retrieval. No adaptive/precision-driven k and no explicit token-budget cap reported.
survey_scope_and_axes: N/A (this is an empirical method paper, not a survey).
benchmark_construction_and_size: N/A (uses existing public datasets; not a new benchmark). Datasets are standard NQ, ANLI-r3, GSM8k, AQuA, StrategyQA.
builds_on: Retrieval-based ICL line: KATE (Liu et al. 2022), EPR (Rubin et al. 2022), CEIL (Ye et al. 2023); GTR dense retriever (Ni et al. 2021); BM25 (Robertson et al. 2009); Chain-of-Thought prompting (Wei et al. 2022b; Wang et al. 2022); base models PaLM (Chowdhery et al. 2022) and Flan-PaLM (Chung et al. 2022). The trained retriever extends EPR-style LM-feedback retriever training.
contrasts_with: Random/fixed-demonstration ICL and zero-shot (no-demo) prompting; off-the-shelf QA/IR retrievers (BM25, GTR) that capture query-specific knowledge but not task-nature; prior retrieval-ICL work focused on general LLMs (e.g., GPT-3) without instruction-tuned models or CoT, and cross-task retrieval methods like UPRISE (Cheng et al. 2023). Also contrasted with implicit-demonstration approaches like RetroPrompt.
lineage: Group A (icl_demonstration_retrieval): a foundational empirical study in the retrieval-augmented in-context-learning lineage, extending retrieval-of-demonstrations from general LLMs to instruction-finetuned LLMs and CoT, and adding a learned (LM-feedback-trained) demonstration retriever. Predecessor-adjacent to EPR/CEIL; precursor to later learned demo-retriever and diverse-coverage selection work.
